claim: The use of excessive force by officers negates probable cause for a lawful arrest under § 148(a)(1) only when the excessive force precedes any refusal to comply with ejection, and where such temporal ambiguity exists, individual officers cannot invoke qualified immunity unless it is clearly established that the violation of § 148(a)(1) was completed prior to the application of force.
initial_reasoning: The cited reporter volume (388 F. Supp. 3d 1158) does not contain language establishing the precise rule that excessive force negates probable cause for a § 148(a)(1) arrest only when it precedes a refusal to comply, nor does it set a qualified‑immunity limitation tied to the timing of the violation. The case discusses related issues but does not provide the specific doctrinal statement required to support the claim.
